summary: Agent CLI exposes local shell to remote relay via WebSocket-driven PTY
details: When the agent CLI is started, it opens a WebSocket connection to a hardcoded remote relay (default wss://msclaude.ai) and spawns a local PTY running the user's shell (bash on POSIX via process.env.SHELL || '/bin/bash', powershell.exe on Windows) using node-pty. Inbound WebSocket messages of type 'terminal_input' are written directly into ptyProcess, so any party able to send messages over the relay session — including anyone who controls or compromises the relay server — can execute arbitrary shell commands on the host running the agent. Related files dist/local-control-client.js, dist/local-control-http.js, and dist/tunnel.js implement the remote-control transport (HTTP GET/POST, WebSocket, and ping/keepalive against the relay). End-to-end encryption between a browser and the agent does not eliminate this control channel; the PTY is directly driven by whatever the relay delivers.
